belief: If I grieve deeply, I don’t trust God.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you grieve deeply you don’t trust God, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Hearing “They’re in a better place, so don’t be sad.” A church culture that expects quick recovery from loss. Feeling pressure to look strong for others. Confusing hope with the absence of sadness. Guilt when tears keep coming months or years later.
teaches: Grief is the price of love, and Scripture does not forbid it. Jesus knew He was about to raise Lazarus, and still He wept. Paul did not tell believers not to grieve, but not to grieve like those without hope. Jesus said those who mourn are blessed, for they will be comforted. God is near to the brokenhearted and keeps track of every tear. Deep grief and deep trust can live in the same heart.
self_statements: If I really trusted God, I wouldn’t be this sad.
I should be over this by now.
I have to be strong for everyone.
I’m letting God down by hurting so badly.
errors: Believing you must either trust God or grieve, but not both.
“I should be over this by now.”
Measuring your grief against how others seem to cope.
Hearing “do not grieve like the rest” as “do not grieve at all.”
questions: Did Jesus weep, even knowing He would raise Lazarus?
What did Paul actually say about grief in 1 Thessalonians 4:13?
What does Jesus promise to those who mourn?
Does God keep track of my tears or scold me for them?
Can I grieve and hope at the same time?
Who told me grief means weak faith?
What kind of comfort do I need right now?
truth: Grieving deeply does not mean I don’t trust God. Jesus wept, and God keeps track of my tears. I can grieve with hope, trusting that God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him. Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You wept at Your friend’s grave. Help me reject the lie that deep grief means I don’t trust God. Keep my tears in Your bottle, comfort me in my sorrow, and let me grieve with hope. In Your name, Amen.
